verdicts.claim: A bug in the played LAN build: a pause's rollback left fight 0 in the state, so a paused PC showed the wrong fight. The fix is parked unfinished with its gates part-run.
verdicts.what_is_true: In a8bc66e2, NetHost.idle calls frame(), which runs session.sync() and can roll back and re-run ticks. NetLan.idle never calls _follow, which only tick() does (lan.gd:99), so a paused 2v2 PC can be left holding fight 0. The fix exists only in the untracked docs/net/pending/lan-n4, where transport_check and the exported --lan-loop rows are 'Not run'. LAN code is absent from the public pin, and the bug is a display fault while paused with no player-harm path.
proof: a8bc66e2:net/lan.gd:3-4 (private builds only; public desktop builds exclude net/)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A LAN view bug sits on the safety ledger even though it can only show the wrong fight while a private build is paused.
verdicts.fix: Move to Netcode's bug queue and finish lan-n4's remaining runs there.

verdicts.claim: Orb reported faults in the LAN and 2v2 tests: intermittent stutter, both screens following only the main PC's fight, crackly audio on high-speed impacts, no sound until the first pause, and fighters clipping into the ground.
verdicts.what_is_true: Orb did say these things. The silence until the first pause comes from the a8bc66e2 play file, and the 2v2 stutter and camera quotes are recorded in vision.md:1660-1663. The crackly audio came from the 2026-11-06 solo play on build 10d8b8cf (vision.md:1654), not from the LAN tests. The ground-clipping quote appears only in vision.md. None of these is a player-safety fault, and none was reproduced.
proof: orb-first-play-20261106-1934.json 'Did the hits sound right?': crackly audio, build 10d8b8cf
orb-first-play-20261107-1229.json: sound not audible until first pause, build a8bc66e2
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Five QA and feel bugs from private tests sit on the safety ledger and compete with real safety work.
verdicts.fix: Move to QA's bug register with Audio, Netcode, Camera and World as owners, and correct the record so the crackle is dated to the 2026-11-06 solo play.

verdicts.claim: GB-001: pressing F9 twice leaves the game permanently grey (split-screen re-attach), and only a restart gets out.
verdicts.what_is_true: This is a stale claim. GB-001 was fixed on 2026-10-01 in 658c95b1 ('F9 grey screen fixed'). attach() now reuses its viewports (split_view.gd:98-103), and pane_check case 8 asserts that attach, detach, attach keeps two panes. The guard is in both the public pin 257a766c and a8bc66e2. F9 is matched as a code string at main.gd:1560, so the search for KEY_F9 was the wrong probe. The register entry was never marked fixed. I did not run pane_check (no Godot).
proof: 257a766c and a8bc66e2 split_view.gd both carry the GB-001 guard
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A fixed bug stays open on the web list and invites a re-fix or a new gate.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record: mark GB-001 fixed in 658c95b1 and name pane_check case 8 as its regression test.

verdicts.claim: The legacy suite (node qa/run-all.js) gates determinism, the seam, and a 1,000-match soak with no NaN, no crash, no fighter outside the world and casualties never above population. Golden hashes are pinned to Node 24, and 'CI should pin the Node version'.
verdicts.what_is_true: I ran the suite: all 7 test files pass on Node v24.19.0, including the 1,000-match soak and the 11 golden hashes. It tests only the legacy HTML prototype and the frozen JS core (run-all.js:2), not the Godot game at /play/. CI already pins Node 24.19.0 (ci.yml:40), but CI has run no job since 3c9005ac, so the suite gates nothing today.
proof: evidence/AC-229.txt (run-all --quick: all 7 passed; --only=soak,determinism: 1000 matches, 0 timeouts, golden 11 match; exit 0)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Listing this suite as a stability gate suggests it soak-tests the shipped Godot game, which it does not.
verdicts.fix: Move to QA's process docs, mark the Node pin done, and stop counting the suite as a release gate for the Godot build.

verdicts.claim: Cross-processor agreement gates the LAN plan: if the two PCs disagree, everything else waits.
verdicts.what_is_true: The gate is written at two-v-two-lan.md:86, and the records disagree. two-pc-check.md:74 says the check has only run on this PC, while lan-v1.md:83 says it ran on both. The old-PC result file shows the i5-6600K ran the check with twopc_exit 0. I did not compare that report against the Ryzen's. A desync is a netcode correctness issue in private LAN builds, not player harm.
proof: oldpc-result-20261101-1813.json: cpu i5-6600K, twopc_exit 0, build dafc348f
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: the stale line can make the LAN plan look blocked on a check that has already run.
verdicts.fix: Correct two-pc-check.md:74 and keep the gate in Netcode's plan rather than the safety records.

verdicts.claim: Known LAN rough edges, with no drop policy for a vanished peer: one match only with no rematch, a lost link just stops, no rejoin, two peers only, a pause holds the other PC, and in 2v2 the other fight is not drawn but can still reach you.
verdicts.what_is_true: In a8bc66e2 no LAN host calls NetSession.dropSlot. A closed link only sets the title to 'The other PC has gone' (lan.gd:246), and rollback.md:312-316 states there is no rejoin and only two peers. SETUP2X turns cross-fight hits on (lan.gd:17), so in 2v2 a blow can come from a fight that is not drawn. LAN is private-only and absent from the public pin. These are missing features and UX issues, not safety ones, and online play comes after launch.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A feature backlog ends up on the safety ledger.
verdicts.fix: Move to Netcode's backlog: build a drop policy and notice before any online release, and send the undrawn-fight hit to Camera and Encounter as a design item.

verdicts.claim: The Godot QA run exits non-zero only if the run broke (no Godot, NaN, a fighter outside the world) or a hard acceptance test failed. Band FAILs fail it only with --fail.
verdicts.what_is_true: Traced as written. The run exits 1 on a bad record (:61-62) or a hard test FAIL (:89), and on band FAILs only with --fail (:99). A missing Godot exits 2. The feel, level, crossing and masher probes catch their own errors and print 'skipped' without failing the run (:72-81), and no workflow runs run-godot.js. This is a QA tool's exit policy, not a release-safety matter.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: it implies a release gate where there is only a manual QA tool.
verdicts.fix: Move to QA's docs. If the run is meant to gate, add it to CI and make skipped probes fail it.

verdicts.claim: Cross-play is only as wide as the parity proof: macOS ARM, Linux ARM, Android and iOS are not proven bit-identical (FMA). The parity gate must run on each, and the web and macOS/ARM must be added to CI before those platforms ship.
verdicts.what_is_true: Every CI job runs on ubuntu-24.04 x64, so macOS and ARM go unchecked, and macOS is a launch platform (ADR 0011:8). ADR 0006:29 is partly stale because web-parity.yml now checks the web build. The FMA risk is plausible but unproven. Android and iOS are parked, and cross-play is post-launch. A desync is a correctness issue, not player harm.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: As a safety gate it could block a macOS release that has no cross-play at launch.
verdicts.fix: Move to Simulation and Netcode as a precondition for cross-platform play and replays, and correct ADR 0006:29 to say the web is now checked.

verdicts.claim: Mutable statics outside the snapshot (DirBrawl._fr*, DirExchange.planEntry and others) are unaudited and could desync only under rollback. DirAlchemy's memo can be read across two fights.
verdicts.what_is_true: The named statics exist, and sim/ holds about 948 non-tool static vars. I spot-checked two. planEntry is set before _start and reset to 0 right after (exchange.gd:201-205). DirAlchemy's memo is keyed by S's id, the tick and the log bits, so a cross-fight read returns what it would compute, if its stated purity holds. The rest are unaudited, and only rollback in private LAN builds could expose them. It is a desync risk, not player harm.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: an engineering audit item sits on the safety ledger.
verdicts.fix: Move to Netcode and Simulation, and write the statics audit (a set-before-read lint for per-tick statics) before online play.

verdicts.claim: Before Orb's first play: the warning shows first, the match record saves even when a match is cut short, ten minutes of sim on several seeds runs with no errors, stuck states or hangs, the median frame is under 16.7 ms, and the exact build is kept outside the repo.
verdicts.what_is_true: The list says this (first-press-list.md:13-17). It was written on 2026-11-01 for Orb's private first play, which has since happened (vision.md:1654-1660). The warning is in force: the photo notice words are in a8bc66e2 terms.json. I found no saved result for the ten-minute run or the 16.7 ms median in docs/ep. It is a spent handover checklist, not a safety record.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Keeping a spent private checklist as a gate implies pass results that were never filed.
verdicts.fix: Retire it as a safety item, and keep it as EP process with its results filed or the list closed.

verdicts.claim: The web build's first start takes 22 to 57 s on this PC and possibly 1.5 to 2.5 minutes on a low-end phone, and the page may look stuck meanwhile.
verdicts.what_is_true: Performance measured 22.8 s at x1 and 57.0 s at a 6x CPU throttle on 257a766c, so '57 s on this PC' is really an emulated slower CPU. The 1.5 to 2.5 minutes is an extrapolation. The live /play/ serves a 38.4 MB wasm and a 9.0 MB pck and shows no start-state line, because the crumbs switch is off (no 'crumbs' key in tools/site.json). A slow start that looks frozen is a UX problem, not player harm.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: it keeps a performance and UX item on the safety ledger.
verdicts.fix: Move to Performance, with Tools for the site switch, and correct the record to say the 57 s was at a 6x throttle.

verdicts.claim: SimCore.dispose leaves a disposed sim's _plans and _jobs behind, a small leak for a host playing many planet matches in one process.
verdicts.what_is_true: This is a stale claim, fixed on 2026-10-30 in fbdbe7b6. SimCore.dispose now calls WorldEpoch.release(S) unless keepWorld is set (sim.gd:38), and release drops the sim's _plans and _jobs. The only keepWorld caller is the rollback restore (net/snapshot.gd:69), where the state plays on. a8bc66e2 includes the fix, and the public pin 257a766c has no epoch.gd at all.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A fixed leak stays listed as open work for World.
verdicts.fix: Retire it: mark it fixed in fbdbe7b6.
